To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the increase in high-level gentamican resistance (HLGR) in invasive Enterococccus faecium in Norwary is associated with hospital-associated genetic lineages carrying HLGR-encoding transferable plasmids.

a 10-fold increased prevalence of high-level aminoglyoside resistance (HLAR) in invasive Enterococci in Norway is associated mainly with major hospital-adaptated lineages carrying transferable aac(6′)-Ie-aph (2″)-Iad-encoding plasmid(s).

the increased prevalence of high-level aminoglycocidic resistance in invasive Enteroccocus faecium in the Norwegian population is associated with major hospital-adaptated genetic lineages carrying an aminoglycocide-modifying enzyme-encoding transferable mega-plasmid.
